summary: Siuslaw National Forest lookout in Lane County, Oregon: cupola in the 1920s, a 41-foot tower in 1954, last staffed 1971, removed about 1975; the site is gone.

facts.design: Treated timber tower, 41 feet, with an L-4 cab (1954); the first lookout was a D-6 cupola
facts.status_note: Removed in 1975 per the register (c.1975 per the Forest Lookouts site); no source describes what remains

events.note: Examiner A.R. Wilcox calls the peak an ideal place for a permanent lookout (Morning Register, Feb. 7, 1923); the item places the mountain in Lincoln County, near Waldport
A lookout spent the summer of 1924 on the peak, per the Eugene Guard (Sept. 27, 1924)
Newspapers of April 1925 describe a new lookout house being erected; a January 1926 item says one was built for $924. The register dates the first D-6 cupola to the 1920s
Walter Hosford named fire lookout for the summer (June 11, 1926 item)
Ed Weise identified as lookout man (Siuslaw Oar, Aug. 15, 1930)
L-4 cab replaced the cupola (register: 1932; firelookout.com: 1934)
Therone Farris and Verus Dahlin shared the season
Activated March 7, 1942, for the Eugene Filter Center
L-4 cab placed on a short tower
41-foot treated timber tower with an L-4 cab. Register says built; the Forest Lookouts site cites a memo on moving the Blodgett Peak lookout; firelookout.com says moved from Blodgett Peak
Used as an emergency post; sold for salvage
Registered November 6, 2019 by Tammy McLeod as FFLOS US 1796

corrections.why: The register gives the first cupola as 1920's, not 1920. Newspapers from April 1925 describe a lookout house being erected, and a January 1926 item says one was built for $924.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says Lane County. A 1923 newspaper item quoted by the Forest Lookouts site says Lincoln County, near Waldport. The record keeps Lane County, which the register gives; the story says the sources disagree.
The register gives 1932 for the L-4 cab; firelookout.com gives 1934. Both are kept in the story and the event note.

The register says a 41-foot tower was built in 1954. The Forest Lookouts site cites a memo estimating the cost of moving the Blodgett Peak lookout to the site. Firelookout.com says the tower was moved from Blodgett Peak. The story reports all three.

notes_for_editor: Gone site: no source describes what remains, or whether the site is open, so the story says so. Sources conflict on the L-4 cab date (1932 vs 1934) and on whether the 1954 tower was built or moved from Blodgett Peak; both are reported. The 1923 county mismatch (Lincoln vs Lane) is reported too. The brief's 1920 build year is not in any source; the register says 1920's and newspapers show 1925-26. The register's 'Administered by' field is U.S. Forest Service. The 2010 site photo credited on the register is captioned only, so no photo record was added. The register registration date (November 6, 2019) is from the register page.
